page.layout: One column of running text, printed page 414. Running head "DESCRIPTIO" at the top. Page number 414 at the top left. Catchword "rum" at the foot right. No margin notes. The red scan edge and the marks at the bottom left are not printed text.

main_text.p: Statimque editi sunt, qui legationem obirent, Callicrates ipse pestis patriae pessima, Lysiades Megalopolitanus, Aratus Sicyonius, & his certa mandata, quibus insisterent, data. Qui Romam cum venissent, Callicrates solus in senatum vocatus, id quod clàm ipse procuraverat, & dicere jussus, neglectis omninò mandatis, in orationem ejusmodi ingressus est, ac si pecuniâ emptus ad prodendam patriae libertatem advenisset. Nec enim solum sententiam senatus, quod facere jussus erat, super eo, super quo inter se dissentiebant Achaei, non inquirebat, nec solum eos, qui à se in republica diffidebant, audaciter coepit accusare, sed etiam ipsum senatum Romanum velut negligentem officii sui commonere, & quid facto opus esset ad [?]umdandum patriae suae jus ac libertatem, docere. Ipsos nimirum Romanos dicebat sibi deesse, & causam dare, cur minus morigeros Græcos haberent, sive aliquid per literas ab ipsis peterent, sive quid imperarent: duas jam esse in omnibus civitatibus popularî statu gaudentibus factiones, quorum altera censeret, obsecundandum Romanis per literas aliquid petentibus, nec ullam legem, ullum fædus etiam columnæ inscriptum, aut aliud quidvis voluntate Romanorum

page.notes: The word after "ad" is blurred: the scan shows a long-s-like form, read here as an unclear word and marked [?]; the probable reading is "pestumdandum" or similar, not certain. "popularî" is copied as printed in the scan (the accent is uncertain). Hyphenated line breaks: "procu-raverat", "ul-lum" joined as "ullum". The printed "rum" at the foot is the completion of "Romanorum" and is recorded as the catchword. Printing error to keep: "dissentiebant" is printed as is. Possible printing errors in "imperarent:duas" (colon spacing as printed).
